label: 2026 Orbital Launches
delta: ~105 Falcon-family launches in 2026 as of Sep 6: Starlink 15-24 (SLC-4E Vandenberg, B1088 19th flight, 27 satellites, 1426 UTC) — SpaceX's 103rd Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and the year's 80th dedicated Starlink mission (tallies for the Falcon-family total, which also counts Falcon Heavy flights, vary slightly by source). No launches occurred Sep 3-5. Previously: 104 Falcon-family launches as of Sep 2: Starlink 15-23 (SLC-4E Vandenberg, B1063 35th flight, 27 V2-Mini satellites, 0842 UTC), the year's 79th Starlink mission. That followed the Aug 30 Falcon Heavy launch of NASA's Roman Space Telescope from LC-39A Kennedy — SpaceX's 102nd Falcon-family orbital launch of 2026 (tallies vary slightly by source) and the sixth NASA flagship-class payload to fly on a Falcon rocket. Previously: 101 launches as of Aug 26 (Starlink 15-22, SLC-4E Vandenberg, B1082 24th flight). The prior launch, Starlink 10-49 (SLC-40 Cape Canaveral, B1067 37th flight — a new reuse record, 0933 UTC Aug 25), was widely reported as SpaceX's 100th Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and was also the company's last planned Falcon 9 Starlink mission from Florida — SpaceX VP of Launch Kiko Dontchev confirmed Florida Starlink deployment now shifts to Starship, with Vandenberg absorbing the bulk of 2026's remaining Starlink cadence. Roughly 75% of 2026's missions have been Starlink. President Gwynne Shotwell projects ~140-145 Falcon 9 launches for the full year (2024: 138 total missions; 2025: 167). Starship IFT-14 (Booster 21 + Ship 41) remains pending; an Aug 31 FCC filing set a Sept 15, 2026 target for the flight, SpaceX's first attempt at reaching full orbital velocity, with roughly 20 operational Starlink V3 satellites on the manifest.

label: Total Booster Recoveries (All-Time)
delta: 659th: OCISLY droneship touchdown (223rd on that vessel) after Starlink 15-24 from Vandenberg (B1088, 19th flight), Sep 6. 658th: OCISLY droneship touchdown after Starlink 15-23 from Vandenberg (B1063, 35th flight), Sep 2. 656th-657th: Falcon Heavy's two side boosters landed simultaneously at Cape Canaveral on the Aug 30 Roman Space Telescope launch — Landing Zone 2 (19th landing on that pad) and Landing Zone 40 (6th) — the center core was expended for extra performance to the Sun-Earth L2 transfer. 655th: OCISLY droneship touchdown (221st on that vessel) after Starlink 15-22 from Vandenberg (B1082, 24th flight), Aug 26. 654th: ASOG droneship touchdown (165th on that vessel) after Starlink 10-49 from Cape Canaveral (B1067, 37th flight — a new single-booster reuse record), Aug 25 — SpaceX's last planned Falcon 9 Starlink landing tied to a Florida launch. Two landings Aug 21: OCISLY (220th on vessel) after Starlink 15-20 from Vandenberg (B1100, 9th flight), and ASOG (164th on vessel) after Starlink 10-39 from Cape Canaveral (B1078, 30th flight). 651st: OCISLY landing after the Aug 19 Starlink Group 17-50 mission from Vandenberg (B1097, 12th flight). 650th: OCISLY landing after the Aug 15 USSF-366 mission from Vandenberg (B1088, 18th flight) — the second half of a record 38.5-minute dual-launch turnaround. 649th (same day): Landing Zone 40 touchdown after the Aug 15 Globalstar 2-R mission from Cape Canaveral (B1090, 14th flight). Note: IFT-12 Booster 19 (May 22) and IFT-13 Booster 20 (July 24) were NOT recovered — both lost during off-nominal landing-burn/splashdown attempts in Gulf of Mexico ocean landings (Starship boosters are not counted in this Falcon-family recovery tally).

label: Starlink Satellites in Orbit
delta: ~11,093 in orbit / ~11,078 operational as of Sep 6, 2026, per Jonathan McDowell's tracking (12,881 launched all-time), reflecting the Sep 2 and Sep 6 Starlink deployments (27 satellites each, Vandenberg) net of ongoing deorbits of older units. Previously: ~11,093 in orbit / ~11,078 working as of Sep 3, 2026. Earlier: ~11,102 in orbit per McDowell as of Aug 27; ~11,050 as of Aug 26 following the Aug 25 Starlink 10-49 (29 sats) and Aug 26 Starlink 15-22 (27 sats) launches — the latter the first Starlink deployment since SpaceX ended Falcon 9 Starlink launches from Florida. SpaceX filed an FCC application July 6 for up to 100,000 Gen3 satellites across two new VLEO shells with W-/D-band frequencies, positioned as AI-data-center backhaul infrastructure in addition to consumer broadband. Aug 4 Q2 earnings: Starlink generated $4.3B of SpaceX's $7.81B quarterly revenue (55% of total).

label: Starlink Subscribers
delta: 12M subscribers per Q2 2026 earnings (Aug 4), up 66% YoY. Starlink revenue $4.3B in Q2 2026 (55% of SpaceX's total). Previously: 10.3M subscribers confirmed in the May 20, 2026 S-1 filing (doubled YoY); Starlink segment profit $1.2B in Q1 2026. 160+ countries served. ARPU: $66/month Q1 2026.

label: Max Single Booster Reflights
delta: B1067 set a new record with its 37th flight on the Starlink 10-49 mission (Aug 25, 2026, SLC-40 Cape Canaveral) — also SpaceX's last planned Falcon 9 Starlink launch from Florida. Previously: 36th flight on Starlink 10-42 (July 9, 2026) — the first orbital booster in history to reach 36 flights; 34th flight on Starlink 10-44 (Mar 30, 2026).

label: Starship Integrated Flight Tests
delta: IFT-14 (Booster 21 + Ship 41) update: an Aug 31 FCC filing requesting Starlink V3 spectrum authorization set Sept 15, 2026 as the target launch/deployment date — the first filing to put a full orbital-insertion profile on Flight 14's paperwork, confirming Musk's Aug 4 earnings-call comment that the flight would carry next-generation V3 satellites (~20 units, ~1 Tbps downlink each) into an operational orbit rather than the short suborbital arcs flown since IFT-6. On Sept 3-4, the FAA issued a Finding of No Significant Impact on its Final Tiered Environmental Assessment for expanded Starship reentry/landing options — a new Northern Pacific contingency area plus expanded Hawaii/Central Pacific and Southeast Pacific contingency zones — giving SpaceX backup splashdown options if the Boca Chica return path or catch tower can't be used; the primary recovery plan for Ship 41 remains an Indian Ocean splashdown, per Musk's Aug 20 comment that a tower catch of the ship is still 'a few months' out rather than on Flight 14. Hardware status: Booster 21 completed a full 33-engine static fire at Pad 2 Aug 28, and underwent a chopsticks lift-and-catch rehearsal on the launch tower Aug 29; Ship 41 completed single-engine (Aug 19) and six-engine (Aug 21) static fires at Massey's Test Site. Remaining steps before Sept 15 are stacking Ship 41 atop Booster 21 and final FAA license sign-off. IFT-13 (Booster 20 V3 + Ship 40 V3) completed July 24, 2026 after a July 16 T-0 abort (6 Raptors flagged low LOX turbopump pressure from moisture; 2 engines replaced before reflight). Results: first-ever deployment of operational satellites — 20 V3 Starlink sats (6 with cameras) released in suborbit and contacted ground stations; Ship 40 relit all 3 Raptors and made a soft Indian Ocean splashdown, remaining intact afterward for the first close-up post-flight heat-shield inspection. Booster 20 was lost on its Gulf of Mexico splashdown attempt — only 10 of 13 landing-burn engines relit, 5 shut down seconds later, causing a hard impact. Prior: FAA cleared Starship to resume flights July 13, 2026, closing the IFT-12 mishap investigation (heat effects on propulsion + erroneous engine alarm settings that prevented Booster 19's reignition, May 22 loss).

label: SPCX (Nasdaq) — Post-IPO Trading
source: SEC EDGAR S-1 / CNBC / Bloomberg / Nasdaq / StockAnalysis.com
contestNote: Trading around $147.32-$150.85 on Sep 6, 2026 (last quote $147.95, down 1.2% intraday), after closing at $149.74 on Sep 4 — up roughly 19% over the trailing 4 weeks and near a post-July high of $149.80 — as the market looks ahead to the Sep 9 Day-90 lock-up tranche (up to 319M more restricted shares eligible to trade) and Starship Flight 14's Sep 15 target date. Previously: closed at $141.50 on Aug 28, 2026 (per Motley Fool), with the next major catalyst a Sept 9 lock-up milestone: up to 319M more restricted shares (~2.4% of shares outstanding, the Day-90 tranche) become eligible to trade, part of a rolling schedule that puts roughly 700M shares (~5.3%) up for potential sale in September and a further ~650M (~4.9%) in October as SpaceX's post-IPO float steps up from under 5% toward a projected 66% by December 2026. Bears (Motley Fool, Investing.com) argue the staggered unlocks could 'swamp retail investors' given SpaceX 'isn't particularly close to recurring profits'; bulls note 75% of the 40 analysts tracked rate the stock a buy with a median 12-month target of $217 (range $75-$800), implying ~53% upside from the Aug 28 close. Aug 24 also brought Musk's confirmation that SpaceX and Nvidia designed a Vera Rubin NVL72 compute system for 'Starmind AI1,' SpaceX's first orbital AI data-center satellite, targeting a Q4 2027 launch — a year earlier than the 2028-earliest timeline SpaceX gave investors in its May 2026 S-1, a gap analysts flagged given the unsolved challenge of radiating hundreds of kilowatts of waste heat in vacuum. That announcement landed the day before SpaceX and Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry announced a $100B 'Starbase Louisiana' spaceport in Vermilion Parish — the same day SpaceX flew its last planned Falcon 9 Starlink launch from Florida (Starlink 10-49, booster B1067's record 37th flight). Traded down as much as 2.1% intraday Monday Aug 24, 2026, changing hands in a roughly $131-$137 range around the $134-$135 level, as the market continued digesting the Aug 4 Q2 print's capex shock ($18.37B in quarterly capex vs. $2.83B a year earlier, mostly AI infrastructure) alongside broader growth-stock headwinds (rising oil prices, geopolitical tension, inflation fears) — SPCX underperformed alongside other richly-valued names on the risk-off day. Prior close was $136.97 on Aug 22, 2026 (+2.2% from the Aug 21 close of $134.00), recovering some ground after trading as low as $132.42 intraday Aug 20, 2026 (down ~5.2% from the prior close), which extended a slide that began as a second major post-IPO lock-up tranche — about 319M restricted shares (~2.4% of shares outstanding, a potential ~20% float increase) — became eligible to trade. SPCX had closed Aug 19 at $139.65, down roughly 2.6-3%, as traders de-risked ahead of the unlock; the reaction diverges from the Aug 6 first-unlock experience, when 911.5M shares hit the float and the stock rose 6% that day and nearly 16% the next. The unlock coincided with confirmation that Starlink generated $4.3B in Q2 2026 revenue (55% of SpaceX's total) on 12M subscribers (+66% YoY), and that the Starlink constellation reached roughly 11,000 satellites in orbit. Bear-case analysts continue to flag traditional valuation models implying fair value as low as $10-30/share. That followed a 4.45% rally to $146.23 on Aug 17 as mid-August 13F filings revealed SpaceX's largest institutional holders for the first time: Alphabet (~551.2M shares, ~$94B), Fidelity (~302.6M shares), Gigafund (~171.8M), Saudi PIF (~154.1M), Nvidia (~122.8M shares, ~$21B, via its xAI stake), and a first-time AMD position (~$565.5M); Harvard Management disclosed ~12.9M shares (~$2.2B) as its largest single U.S. equity holding. Earlier: SPCX fell 3.88% on Aug 14 — underperforming the 2.28%-down Telecommunications Services sector — as SpaceX's $60B all-stock closing of the Anysphere (Cursor) acquisition added ~391M new Class A shares to a market already digesting post-lockup supply. That interrupted a rally that had carried the stock from a 52-week low of $104.83 (Aug 3) to $146.15 intraday (Aug 13, +9.65% that day, driven by a filing showing Musk's 48.4% stake worth over $900B). Earlier in the window: Aug 6 lock-up expiration released up to 911.5M insider shares (~$100B) without triggering a sell-off (+6.1%); shares jumped 15.8% Aug 7-8 on the Q2 earnings beat and the $16.8B Terafab chip-plant confirmation; reclaimed the $135 IPO price Aug 10 (+4%); and surged 9.6% Aug 12 after Musk said AI/Grok revenue could overtake Starlink and launch revenue within 1-2 months. IPO recap: priced at $135/share June 11 (largest IPO in history, $1.77T implied valuation); all-time high $225.64 June 16; joined Nasdaq-100 July 7. Musk holds ~42-48% economic equity (filings vary by measurement date and post-Cursor dilution), ~79-85% voting control (dual-class Class B) — cannot be removed as director except by his own vote.
